acts: RFC 9700, Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security

en.title: OpenID Connect Core: does the exact redirect URI match of Section 3.1.2.1 give way to the loopback port rule of RFC 8252?
en.summary: Section 3.1.2.1 of OpenID Connect Core 1.0 requires the redirect URI to match a registered value exactly. RFC 8252 Section 7.3, published later, requires accepting any port for loopback IP redirect URIs, and RFC 9700 keeps that as the only exception to exact matching. Section 3.1.2.2 says the provider validates OAuth 2.0 parameters according to the OAuth 2.0 specification, so the port rule may already apply through it; the text does not say which sentence controls.
en.impact: A native app registers http://127.0.0.1/cb and sends http://127.0.0.1:51004/cb: under Section 3.1.2.1 the provider must reject it; under RFC 8252 it must accept it.
en.correction: Add a pointer to Section 3.1.2.1: allow the RFC 8252 port exception for loopback IP redirect URIs and refer to RFC 9700 Section 2.6 for the scheme rule.

An AI coordinator checked the place against the full text, the corrections already reported to the RFC Editor and the issue trackers, and two further AI models checked the report before it was sent.
